primary_waste_streams: Drill cuttings; brine from core extraction; diesel exhaust from exploration rigs; disturbed soil and vegetation from access roads
omega_derivation_note: Low absolute waste volume but high habitat disturbance per unit of eventual output; exploration rarely involves process chemicals. Weight set low relative to production phases.

primary_waste_streams: Waste rock (overburden); tailings slurry; acid mine drainage (AMD); particulate dust; blasting NOx; cyanide or mercury at artisanal sites; diesel exhaust from heavy machinery; land clearance and habitat loss
omega_source: Foran 2005 (direct ops 13% + land prep 6% of sector GHG); Newmont 2024 SR (land reclaimed 192 ha/yr; 24% of suppliers flagged for human rights risk); WGC 2019 Climate Report
omega_derivation_note: Largest single waste-intensity phase. Tailings volume dominates (100-200 t waste rock per oz Au). Foran GHG split places direct + land at ~19% of sector; Newmont reclamation data confirms ongoing land obligation. Weight elevated to reflect tailings mass.

primary_waste_streams: Cyanide solution (heap leach or tank leach); mercury vapour (ASGM); acid effluent; process water with heavy metals; flotation reagents; sulfur dioxide from roasting; cyanide spill risk; thickener underflow
omega_source: Foran 2005 (electricity 44% of sector GHG — majority consumed here); Newmont 2024 SR (30 cyanide spills/yr; water recycled 71%); WGC 2019 Climate Report
omega_derivation_note: Highest energy-intensity phase (cyanide leach + grinding). Electricity share of GHG (44%) is concentrated primarily in phases 2-3. Cyanide management is the dominant acute hazard. Highest omega_p in chain.

primary_waste_streams: Smelter slag; sulfur dioxide and NOx from furnace; acid pickling effluent; mercury capture waste; spent refractories; heat and water vapour
omega_source: Foran 2005 (electricity share partly here); Newmont 2024 SR (cyanide spills note Phase 2-3 boundary); industry LCA benchmarks
omega_derivation_note: Smelting is energy- and emissions-intensive but shorter duration than leach. Slag volume is significant (1-5 t slag per t doré). Placed below Phase 2 given shorter process time and smaller effluent volume.

primary_waste_streams: Acid pickling liquors (nitric and sulfuric); chlorine gas (Miller process); electrolyte slimes (anode slime with PGMs); cooling water discharge; spent electrolyte; minor emissions of chlorine and HCl
omega_source: Industry LCA benchmarks; LBMA Responsible Sourcing Guidance 2021
omega_derivation_note: Refinery waste volumes are smaller than extraction phases but chemically aggressive. Acid liquors require neutralisation. PGM-bearing anode slimes are a recoverable by-product but also a waste stream until processed.

primary_waste_streams: Metal shavings and filings (recoverable); cutting lubricants and grinding coolant; electroplating rinse water; assay cupel waste (lead, silver); packaging materials
omega_derivation_note: Relatively low waste intensity. Metal filings are largely recovered. Assay waste (cupels, lead buttons) is a known regulated stream. Energy consumption mainly from annealing and casting furnaces.

primary_waste_streams: Diesel exhaust from armoured transport; climate-control energy (HVAC for vault temperature); packaging and desiccant waste; security hardware end-of-life
omega_source: Industry estimates; Newmont 2024 SR transport emissions
omega_derivation_note: Near-zero material waste. Primary environmental cost is HVAC energy for vault climate control and transport fuel. Placed low as no process chemicals or transformation occur.

primary_waste_streams: Data centre energy (electronic record systems); paper documentation and packaging waste; negligible physical waste
omega_derivation_note: Essentially zero physical waste. Environmental cost is limited to digital infrastructure energy. Lowest omega_p in chain by a large margin.
